ig_caption:
Your kids help with the business? Paid the right way, a child can earn up to $16,100 in 2026 with no federal income tax.

✔️ Their own 2026 standard deduction covers wages up to $16,100 when they have no other income.
✔️ Under 18 and working for a parent's sole proprietorship (or a partnership owned only by the parents): no Social Security or Medicare tax.
✔️ If the business is a corporation, the usual payroll taxes apply at any age.
✔️ The work has to be real and the pay fair for the job. Pay by Dec 31 to count for 2026, keep timesheets and pay by transfer.

State rules vary. We check if it fits your business in a year-end session.

li_caption:
If your children do real work in your business, paying them a fair wage can move income from your tax bracket to theirs. The rules depend on how the business is set up.

1. A child's 2026 standard deduction covers wages up to $16,100 when they have no other income, so those wages carry no federal income tax.
2. A child under 18 working for a parent's sole proprietorship, or a partnership where each partner is a parent, is not subject to Social Security or Medicare tax on those wages. Under 21, no federal unemployment tax either.
3. If the business is a corporation, including an S corp you own, the usual payroll taxes apply at any age.
4. The pay must be reasonable and for services actually performed. Run it through payroll, issue a W-2, keep timesheets and pay by transfer.
5. For a cash-basis business, wages count for 2026 only if they are paid by Dec 31.

State rules vary. In a year-end planning session we check whether this fits your business and what the job and pay should look like.

sources.fact: Child under 18 employed by parent's sole proprietorship or partnership where each partner is a parent: not subject to Social Security and Medicare; under 21 not subject to FUTA; subject to income tax withholding regardless of age; corporation: all taxes apply regardless of age (page updated 11-Oct-2026, read 2026-11-12)
2026 standard deduction single $16,100; dependent's standard deduction = greater of $1,350 or earned income + $450, capped at the regular amount (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sec. 4.14, read 2026-11-12)
Employees' pay deductible if ordinary and necessary, reasonable, for services performed, and paid or incurred in the tax year; Form W-2 reports wages to employees (Pub 334, read 2026-11-12)
